The Internet has replaced many newspapers as the principal source of information as newspapers' popularity has declined. People have access to a variety of news
sources on the Internet. The tremendous increase in everyday internet users has resulted from the decreased cost of internet services. The number of Internet users
in India has increased by about 146% in the last five years. The most common news sources today are social media, despite the fact that
online newspapers were once very popular. Creating content and disseminating it to the public under the guise of true news from a reliable news source
is a major concern. This has led to an increase in the frequency with which people consume 'false news.' The dissemination of fake news has
severe consequences, including the potential to influence election outcomes. This research focuses on using crowdsourcing to address the challenge of recognising bogus news on the
Internet. Crowdsourcing is the practise of gathering data from a sizable number of people, usually online. An efficient method for crowdsourcing fact-checking has been revealed
by prior research. In order to stop the spread of false information on the Internet, aims to solve the limitations of earlier research studies and
build on them to make crowdsourcing a reliable method for fact-checking. concludes with an order for a person to be verified in a specific category,
they will need to post several comments and reviews that are continuously scored highly. This requirement ensures the authenticity of authenticated users and the fact-checking
they do. © 2023 IEEE.

In the current digital era, the popularity of social media platforms has expanded tremendously. Every one of us, no matter what age or gender or
class we belong to, are active on social media, sharing so much of our personal and professional life with the world. We are connected with
people, countries and borders apart via our phone now. News companies are also recognizing this change in the world and are now making business through
this by publishing information online. The rapid spread of an article on the internet by the normal public without checking for its authenticity is resulting
in a surge in the amount of incorrect information available online. No end-user finds it simple to confirm the veracity of a given news article.
These fake articles are increasing rapidly and making it far more difficult for the real information to reach the public. The purpose of is to
develop an efficient model for assessing the credibility of a news article. addresses the classification problem of Fake News, given just the news article's content
and the author's name. The system proposed in works with Hierarchical Convolutional-Attention Network (HCAN) and Convolutional Neural Network to classify the fake news articles based
on the words and phrases used in the published piece. Hierarchical Convolutional-Attention Network (HCAN) is comprised of attention-enhanced word-level and sentence-level encoders as well as
a to capture sequential correlation. We have also used Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) for word encoder and sentence encoder in our system. We carried out
the experiment on our system using a dataset and compared the results with various baseline models like , RCNN, BERT or LR. Extensive trials demonstrate
that HCAN outperforms the most advanced baseline models on a collected dataset. Results of our experiment shows that our model is achieving the F1 score
of 0.98. © 2023 IEEE.

The digital era is proliferating, and we are in a time where we interact with lots of information in many ways. Life has become more
sensitive with social media, and in the present scenario, users’ activity on social media has become more frequent. The impact of social media and the
news shared over it directly impacts the user. Social media is a powerful tool that can spread word of mouth in a fraction of a
second. There is a variety of content and information shared all over social media and other information sources. This mystifies the user to agree on
whether it is genuine or fake news. Social media has given so much power to the user that they immediately start expressing their views and
concerns without checking the authenticity of the posted content. As a result, the user shares the news and becomes a spreader of fake news. This
is a challenging task for the government and the country’s citizens. The most popular form of unauthenticated information is rumors and fake news, and this
should be combated as early as possible before it takes any dramatic consequence. For this, we propose a solution where a long short term memory(LSTM)
model is used to detect the fake news, and the proposed approach attained the accuracy of 98%. © 2023, The Author(s), under exclusive license to
Springer Nature Switzerland AG.

Social media refers to communication channels on Internet that enable the creation and publication of content generated by the user and interaction between users. Given
the accessibility to these means of communication and their rapidity, people resort more to them comparatively to the traditional media including radio, television and newspapers.
However, dubious pieces of information such as fake news are often disseminated for malicious purposes. The proliferation of fake news has a strong negative impact
on a society such as damage to the reputation of a personality, an organization or the aggravation of conflicts between its members. Due to the
proliferation of fake news on these websites, the notion of veracity of information becomes a crucial issue. Research based on machine learning is promising. However,
one of the main limitations is the efficiency of predictions. As a solution to detect fake news, we have proposed two models based on hybrid
deep learning and evaluated our models on the two real datasets, namely ISOT and FA-KES. An experience of the proposed models to detect fake news,
allowed to obtain on ISOT an accuracy of 99% for both models and on FA-KES, we obtain an accuracy of 68% for one the models
and an accuracy of 63% for other. Other experiments in generalizing models on these data sets have proposed. The results obtained are better than other
machine learning models. © 2023 by the authors.

Social media is a popular medium for the dissemination of real-time news all over the world. Easy and quick information proliferation is one of the
reasons for its popularity. An extensive number of users with different age groups, gender, and societal beliefs are engaged in social media websites. Despite these
favorable aspects, a significant disadvantage comes in the form of fake news, as people usually read and share information without caring about its genuineness. Therefore,
it is imperative to research methods for the authentication of news. To address this issue, this article proposes a two-phase benchmark model named WELFake based
on word embedding (WE) over linguistic features for fake news detection using machine learning classification. The first phase preprocesses the data set and validates the
veracity of news content by using linguistic features. The second phase merges the linguistic feature sets with WE and applies voting classification. To validate its
approach, this article also carefully designs a novel WELFake data set with approximately 72 000 articles, which incorporates different data sets to generate an unbiased
classification output. Experimental results show that the WELFake model categorizes the news in real and fake with a 96.73% which improves the overall accuracy by
1.31% compared to bidirectional encoder representations from transformer (BERT) and 4.25% compared to convolutional neural network () models. Our frequency-based and focused analyzing writing patterns
model outperforms predictive-based related works implemented using the Word2vec WE method by up to 1.73%. © 2014 IEEE.

Social media has become the backbone of today's lifestyle. It has a widespread effect on nearly every walk of life. One of the well-known social
media applications WhatsApp Messenger is a free and cross-platform text messaging software that also provides services for sending and receiving multimedia messages. But at the
same time in recent years, its easy accessibility has served a way for propagating fake and biased news articles, blogs and messages. Fake news and
messages have paved their way for Political polarization, ethnic tensions, unwanted panic and mass hysteria. A solution is proposed that uses Natural Language Processing for
analyzing the messages and leverage Transfer Learning Models to detect the authenticity of the information. Claims are filtered from the bulk of forwarded messages disseminated
on WhatsApp. The solution comprises of a semantic search mechanism between each claim and associated news sources. The similarity comparison done by the model predicts
the truthfulness of the claim. © 2020 IEEE.
